source_text: Ὁ δὲ μακάριος Πόθεινος, ὁ τὴν διακονίαν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς ἐν Λουγδούνῳ πεπιστευμένος, ὑπὲρ τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἔτη τῆς ἡλικίας γεγονώς, καὶ πάνυ ἀσθενὴς τῷ σώματι, μόλις μὲν ἐμπνέων διὰ τὴν προκειμένην σωματικὴν ἀσθένειαν, ὑπὸ δὲ προθυμίας πνεύματος ἀναρρωννύμενος διὰ τὴν ἐγκειμένην τῆς μαρτυρίας ἐπιθυμίαν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα ἐσύρετο, τοῦ μὲν σώματος καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ γήρως καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς νόσου λελυμένου, τηρουμένης δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς ἐν αὐτῷ, ἵνα δι᾽ αὐτῆς Χριστὸς θριαμβεύσῃ· ὃς ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα κομισθείς, παραπεμπόντων αὐτὸν τῶν πολιτικῶν ἐξουσιῶν καὶ παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, ἐπιβοήσεις παντοίας ποιουμένων ὡς αὐτοῦ ὄντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀπεδίδου τὴν καλὴν μαρτυρίαν. Ἀνεταζόμενος δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος τίς εἴη Χριστιανῶν ὁ θεός, ἔφη· Ἐὰν ᾖς ἄξιος, γνώσῃ. Ἐντεῦθεν δὲ ἀφειδῶς ἐσύρετο καὶ ποικίλας ἔπασχε πληγάς, τῶν μὲν σύνεγγυς χερσὶν καὶ ποσὶν ἐνυβριζόντων παντοίως, μηδὲ τὴν ἡλικίαν αἰδουμένων αὐτοῦ, τῶν δὲ μακράν, ὃ μετὰ χεῖρας ἕκαστος εἶχεν, εἰς αὐτὸν ἀκοντιζόντων, πάντων δὲ ἡγουμένων μεγάλως πλημμελεῖν καὶ ἀσεβεῖν, εἴ τις ἀπολειφθείη τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν ἀσελγείας· καὶ γὰρ τοὺς θεοὺς αὐτῶν ᾤοντο οὕτως ἐκδικήσειν. Καὶ μόγις ἐμπνέων ἐρρίφη ἐν τῇ εἱρκτῇ καὶ μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας ἐξέπνευσεν.
pass_a_gloss: But the blessed Pothinus, the one entrusted with the service of the episcopate at Lugdunum, having become beyond ninety years in age and very weak in body, with difficulty indeed breathing because of the bodily weakness set before him, but being made strong again by eagerness of spirit because of the pressing desire for martyrdom, was himself also dragged to the tribunal, his body loosened both by old age and by sickness, but his soul still kept in him in order that through it Christ might triumph; who, carried to the tribunal by soldiers while the civic powers conducted him and all the crowd made shouts of every kind as though he himself were the Christ, rendered back the good martyrdom. And questioned by the governor who the god of the Christians might be, he said: If you are worthy, you will know. From there he was dragged unsparingly and suffered varied blows, those near insulting in every way with hands and feet, not even respecting his age, those far off hurling at him whatever each had in hand, and all reckoning it a great fault and impiety if anyone fell short of licentious outrage against him; for they supposed thus to avenge their gods. And scarcely breathing he was cast into prison and after two days expired.
pass_b_english: The blessed Pothinus, who had been entrusted with the ministry of oversight at Lyons, was past ninety years of age and very frail in body, scarcely breathing because of the bodily weakness that lay upon him, yet revived by eagerness of spirit because of the pressing desire for testimony, and he too was dragged to the tribunal, his body loosed by both age and sickness, but his life still kept in him so that through him Christ might triumph (cf. 2 Corinthians 2:14). Carried to the tribunal by the soldiers, while the civic authorities escorted him and the whole crowd raised cries of every kind as if he himself were the Christ, he rendered the noble testimony (1 Timothy 6:13). When the governor examined him as to who the God of the Christians is, he said, If you are worthy, you will know.

From that point he was dragged without mercy and suffered blows of every kind, those standing near insulting him in every way with hands and feet and showing no respect for his age, while those at a distance hurled at him whatever each had in hand, and all reckoned it a great offense and impiety if anyone fell short in outrage against him, for they supposed that in this way they would avenge their gods. Still barely breathing, he was thrown into prison and after two days breathed his last.

lemmas.gloss: blessed, here honorific for a martyr
being revived, made strong again in spirit
might triumph, display victory through him
to avenge, exact vengeance for their gods

choices.why: kalos with martyria in a judicial confession context means noble or excellent witness rather than morally good, and apodidonai points to rendering formal testimony before the governor

choices.term: τηρουμένης δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς ἐν αὐτῷ
choices.english: but his life still kept in him
choices.why: psyche contrasted with loosened soma in an aged sick man denotes bare life remaining, not soul as theological subject, explaining why he could still be dragged out
rejected: while his soul was preserved within him

choices.why: aselgeia with eis plus description of blows and missiles denotes wanton insolent abuse, not sexual licence, in mob violence

bible_refs.note: τὴν καλὴν μαρτυρίαν echoes τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν / μαρτυρίαν before rulers
ἵνα δι᾽ αὐτῆς Χριστὸς θριαμβεύσῃ echoes θριαμβεύοντι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ
